A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

comment.comment:
$GO
has fallen hard. I'm still holding, and I'm not afraid to say that publicly.

I meant what I wrote about
@lesgodotfun
when the mood was better. I still mean it today.

Of course I care about the price. It's my money in this too. But before I change my position, I want to understand what has changed in the reasons I bought it.

LESGO caught my attention because it has a character people can recognise and a platform that gives creators room to build around it. I can see that identity growing into games, useful tools and communities with a life beyond launch day. That potential still interests me.

There is also a concrete economic connection. According to LESGO's docs, 60% of platform revenue goes into buying and burning GO. If the platform attracts lasting trading activity, that activity can fund continued buybacks.

At a lower price, the same buyback budget can buy more GO. But the budget depends on revenue. That is why I care so much about whether creators and users keep coming back. A burn mechanism needs a business behind it.

This is where I want the team to focus: help promising projects get discovered, make the platform easier to use, support builders after they launch, and show the results openly. Give people enough reasons to stay that they bring someone else.

A few projects that people still use a month later would give me more confidence than a busy launch page for one afternoon.

And we can help with that. Try what's being built. Give useful feedback. Share something because you actually enjoyed it. Bring an idea worth developing. I want to contribute to that kind of community.

I don't know where the bottom is. I also won't pretend every project that falls eventually recovers. LESGO has to earn its future through execution, and I will keep judging it on that.

But I still see something here worth backing. I still see room for a recognisable brand and a stronger ecosystem to grow from this.

My confidence comes with expectations. I can give the team time while continuing to ask for progress. Those two things belong together.

I'm comfortable standing by my view before the outcome is obvious. That's the risk I've chosen to take.

Still here. Still thinking long term. Let's make the next chapter worth staying for.

@lesgodotfun

$GO

comment.comment: Agent Wormhole (WORM): WORM is the security tollbooth for autonomous agents: it protects agent configuration files, blocks manipulated x402 payments and signs token metadata so later changes invalidate the attestation. Its main competitors are Blockaid and Hypernative for transaction protection, Lakera/Prompt Security for prompt-injection defense, and GoPlus/Forta for on-chain security—but Wormhole uniquely combines these surfaces into agent-native, pay-per-scan infrastructure. Each protection call generates a micropayment used for buybacks and burns; the protocol reports 961,682 scans, $14,425 spent and 37.6M WORM burned. A 10× rerating from approximately $1.6M to $16M requires third-party launchpads and agent frameworks producing organic scans—not self-generated traffic. The major near-term catalyst is Wormbook, its planned agent/human launchpad, social network and trading floor; I assign October 24, 2026 as the evaluation date—not an official deadline—by which a public beta or named launchpad integration should demonstrate whether WORM can become embedded security infrastructure rather than a standalone tool.
